assessment.nobel_worthiness: Combines new data and credible empirical designs with an explanatory framework. The task and skill-bias view of technology and the import-competition shock evidence changed how economists and policymakers understand labour demand, wage inequality and the local costs of trade. It has also inspired a large body of follow-on work.
assessment.attribution: Autor is central to both the technology and trade-shock strands. Hanson is the main trade and regional-labour-market partner on the China shock. Katz anchors the long-run skill-demand and supply framework. Dorn is a major co-author on the China shock papers, so a three-name limit leaves a real attribution difficulty. Task-model co-originators such as Levy and Murnane are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Mature. The core papers are from the 1990s to early 2010s and have been replicated, extended and debated for more than a decade, including critiques of the China shock identification and persistence.
uncertainties: Whether Dorn should replace Katz or Hanson
Scope of the technology and trade strands versus a single theme
Robustness of the shock-based estimates and long-run persistence
The task-model antecedents are not on the list

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Kiyotaki-Moore credit-cycles model is a foundational mechanism: collateral constraints amplify and propagate shocks. It underlies a large share of modern macro-finance and policy analysis of financial crises. The contribution is conceptual, tractable and highly influential.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore's 1997 paper is the clear origin and the pair is well defined. Gertler and Gilchrist's financial accelerator work, building on Bernanke, is related but conceptually distinct, so a narrower laureate set is cleaner.
assessment.maturity: Very mature. Nearly three decades of influence, with renewed relevance after 2008, and the empirical and quantitative literature has since confirmed the importance of financial frictions.
uncertainties: Overlap with Bernanke-Gertler-Gilchrist and the earlier Bernanke Nobel
Whether the committee prefers a broader macro-finance prize
Empirical identification of collateral channels is indirect

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Built the leading framework for the political economy of trade policy, the Grossman-Helpman protection-for-sale model. Their wider work on trade, innovation and growth also had lasting theoretical impact, and the framework has been tested empirically.
assessment.attribution: The partnership is clear and long-standing, and the pair is a natural unit. Helpman also appears in the firm-heterogeneity candidate, which overlaps the trade field.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with more than three decades of use and extensive empirical testing. Overall maturity is high, and the main caveat is that trade has been recognised before.
uncertainties: Competition from the firm-heterogeneity trade candidate, which shares Helpman
Mixed empirical support for the protection-for-sale specification
Whether the committee prefers the political-economy or the firm-level trade contribution

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Uses tax records and national accounts to build long-run series on top incomes and wealth, creating a new empirical base for inequality research, in the tradition of archival data discovery. It reshaped research and policy debate on distribution, taxation and offshore wealth. Measurement validity and the explanatory framework are still contested, and the judgement must rest on scientific contribution, not political salience.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez pioneered the top-income series. Zucman extended the work to wealth and tax havens. Atkinson, now deceased, was an important precursor and co-originator. Saez also appears in public-economics work.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature for the income series. The wealth-distribution and offshore-wealth estimates are more recent and methodologically debated.
uncertainties: Contested measurement of wealth shares and the effect of imputations
Explanatory framework (r>g) is disputed
Risk of politically driven assessment rather than scientific merit
Atkinson's role as precursor

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative data gave credible estimates of intergenerational mobility, neighbourhood effects and the long-run effects of exposure to place. It is a major empirical advance in labour and public economics, with strong policy influence and methods now widely adopted.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the leading figure, with Hendren on neighbourhood effects and Friedman on teacher value-added and mobility. Katz, a co-author on Moving to Opportunity, has strong claims elsewhere. The collective-credit boundaries are blurred by many co-authors.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature. The mobility atlas and neighbourhood-effects work is about a decade old, with replications and critiques of the causal interpretation of place effects still developing.
uncertainties: Whether a 2026 prize is premature relative to a later one
Debate on the causal interpretation of place effects and the sensitivity of the mobility estimates
Large team credit, which complicates the three-name limit

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The BLP demand-estimation approach and the Pakes dynamic-oligopoly and estimation work made structural IO empirically operational. They are used widely in merger analysis, antitrust, trade and other applied fields, so the contribution is methodological with deep practical uptake.
assessment.attribution: Pakes (with Berry and Levinsohn), plus Bresnahan and Reiss on empirical IO foundations, form a well-defined set but exceed three names. Pakes's dynamic-model contributions and BLP are partly distinct strands, and the selection is a judgement on core credit.
assessment.maturity: Very mature. Three decades of application and refinement, with ongoing improvements in computation and identification.
uncertainties: How to split credit among Pakes, Berry, Levinsohn and Bresnahan
Sensitivity of results to functional-form and instrument assumptions
Whether the committee views this as method or as a discovery about economics

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The résumé correspondence study of racial name discrimination gave an influential measurement design for labour-market discrimination, widely replicated and extended, with large influence on research and policy debate. The result is a clear empirical finding, and the contribution to theory is more limited.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan's 2004 audit paper is the identifiable core. Charles's contribution lies in related work on racial discrimination and cannot be credited to the same study. Earlier audit-study pioneers and the foundational discrimination theory (Becker, Arrow, Phelps) are separate.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with a 20-year replication record across countries. Interpretation of what the callback gaps measure (taste, statistical discrimination, productivity signals) remains debated.
uncertainties: Narrowness of a single-paper design relative to a career-level prize
Interpretation of callback gaps
Antecedent audit-study work and the wider discrimination literature
Mullainathan's other work spans several subfields

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Established that reciprocity and fairness preferences matter systematically for incentives, contracting and cooperation, via the Fehr-Schmidt inequity-aversion model and a long experimental programme. It has had a significant effect on contract theory, public goods and labour-market behaviour. Prior Nobels for behavioural and experimental economics reduce the marginal case.
assessment.attribution: Fehr is the most identifiable figure, and Schmidt is the theoretical co-originator of the inequity-aversion model. Falk is a major collaborator. Rabin and others developed related fairness models and are credited elsewhere.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with two decades of replication. Lab-to-field external validity and model identification are debated.
uncertainties: Priority relative to Rabin's fairness models
External validity of lab social-preference measures
Adjacent prior recognition of behavioural and experimental economics
